title: New Orleans without a wrong side of the tracks
summary: Reel 2 begins with movie pianists, then neighbourhoods had no railroad-avenue divide and people rented homes.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: We're talking about the different movie pianists. Do you remember any others?
Well, right offhand, no, I sure don't.
You say Tolls played bass? It was bass player. And you were playing trumpet?
I was just a kid then. Oh, just about six, seven, eight pieces. The regular bands like they had around here.
Did you ever hear of anything like that? Is there a Railroad Avenue in New Orleans?
Yeah. You go to all these little towns that have a Railroad Avenue.
Right, I never heard of it. The other side of the track.
There's no such thing as the other side of the tracks in New Orleans.
In those days it weren't. I can't remember it being. Well, in other words, you're trying to see a segregating place as such as the other cities. No, yeah.
I don't remember New Orleans as ever having any slimes until the government made it.
Well, no, like I say, people lived all over the city of New Orleans. I guess that's because of the melting pot that's been here.
Yeah, it always strikes me that every neighborhood had its own character. Right. A lot of people owned their own homes.

I don't know about owning a home so much in the old days. Everybody would rent as well. For instance, this house where I was born, my brother lives in it now. It's just been handed down from my daddy to him. And they don't own the first nail any. They're still paying rent. But like today, it's a different day and time. And people are owning their own homes now.
